title: A password reset whose answer from the provider is lost is never reported as a refused code
assertion: The confirmation of a reset is sent to the provider once, by a client set to one attempt, so a repeat never meets its own used code; an answer that changed nothing stays what it was (one refusal for every code problem, the policy's refusal, a refused client credential), and anything else (no answer, a server fault, a trigger's failure) is an unknown outcome, whether or not the provider applied the reset; on an unknown outcome the person is answered that sign-in could not continue and to start again, never that the code did not match, and the step ends; when the address names an account, one transaction as that account, retried once, takes its row lock, ends its sessions and records `password_reset_outcome_unknown` (purpose `unverified_code`), on which the database moves the mark and ends the sessions, and the provider then signs the user out; no password-changed email is queued; `security event: password reset outcome unknown` is logged at error with the user's ID or none, the request's ID and the provider error's name only, and pages the operator at one in five minutes (`PasswordResetOutcomeUnknown`); an address with no account records nothing and still logs the line; a transaction that fails twice is logged as sessions not ended
noFileReason: A synthetic persona confirms a reset through a provider twin that loses its answer, and the Cognito classification runs on a fake client; no file.
